title: Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan
about: A company of Australian and New Zealand soldiers fight outnumbered in a rubber plantation in Vietnam.

    StartersNui Dat concert night satay skewersLemongrass chicken skewers with peanut satay sauceHow to make it600g chicken thigh fillets1 lemongrass stalk1 tsp ground turmeric2 garlic cloves1 tbsp fish sauce2 tbsp brown sugar150g crunchy peanut butter200ml coconut milk1 tbsp soy sauce1 tsp chilli flakes2 limes1 Lebanese cucumberDice the chicken and toss with chopped lemongrass, turmeric, garlic, fish sauce and brown sugar.Marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.Thread onto skewers.Grill, turning.Simmer the peanut butter, coconut milk, soy, brown sugar, chilli and lime juice into a satay sauce.Serve with cucumber and lime wedges.Phuoc Tuy prawn rice paper rollsFresh rolls of prawn, vermicelli, carrot and cucumberHow to make it100g rice vermicelli12 cooked king prawns1 carrot1 Lebanese cucumber12 rice paper sheets1 bunch of mint1 bunch of coriander3 tbsp fish sauce2 limes2 tbsp caster sugar1 garlic clove1 red chilliSoak the vermicelli in hot water, then drain.Halve the prawns lengthways.Julienne the carrot and cucumber.Dip the rice paper sheets one at a time in warm water for a few seconds.Lay prawns, noodles, vegetables, mint and coriander on each and roll tightly.Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, water, garlic and chilli for dipping.MainsD Company field kitchen beef and beansSlow-cooked beef, cannellini beans and paprika over buttered riceHow to make it800g chuck steak2 tbsp vegetable oil1 onion2 garlic cloves1 red capsicum2 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp ground cumin400g crushed tomatoes (tin)400ml beef stock400g cannellini beans (tin)300g long grain rice20g butter1 jar of pickled chilliesDice the chuck, onion, capsicum and garlic.Brown the beef in batches in oil.Add the onion, garlic and capsicum and cook.Stir in the paprika, cumin, crushed tomatoes, stock and drained cannellini beans.Cover and simmer until tender.Cook the rice and stir through the butter.Serve with sliced pickled chilli.Vung Tau leave caramel porkThree days' leave down at Vung TauHow to make it1kg pork belly, skin off80g brown sugar3 tbsp fish sauce500ml coconut water3 red Asian shallots3 garlic cloves4 eggs300g jasmine rice1 Lebanese cucumber3 spring onions1 red chilliBoil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool and peel. Cut the pork into 4cm pieces.Melt the sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat until dark amber, then stir in the sliced shallots and garlic.Add the pork and toss for 5 minutes, then add the fish sauce and coconut water.Simmer gently, half covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes, adding the eggs for the last 20 minutes, until the pork is tender and the sauce sticky.Simmer the rice with 450ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5.Serve with the rice, sliced cucumber, spring onion and chilli.SweetsRation pack chocolate orange potsDark chocolate cream pots scented with orangeHow to make it400ml thickened cream2 oranges200g dark chocolate2 tbsp caster sugar4 shortbread biscuitsHeat the cream with the orange zest until steaming.Pour over the chopped chocolate, leave to melt and stir until smooth.Stir in the orange juice.Pour into small glasses.Chill for 2 hours.Simmer thin strips of orange zest in sugar and water.Top the pots with whipped cream, the candied zest and crumbled shortbread.DrinksNui Dat Vietnamese iced coffeeStrong dark-roast coffee with condensed milk over iceHow to make it60g dark-roast ground coffee8 tbsp condensed milk1 bag of iceBrew very strong dark-roast coffee, using a Vietnamese phin filter if you have one or a plunger at double strength.Spoon condensed milk into each glass.Pour the hot coffee over and stir until creamy.Fill with ice and stir again until cold.
